summary: The PRD has more binary verify steps than most — AC-3, AC-5, AC-7 cite concrete shell commands, and the existing skill `eval:` field is present. But several ACs leak judgement-laden phrases ("documented HTML shape", "visually distinct shapes", "appears verbatim", "compiles to a `<pre>` element with the literal text 'Unsupported visual block' preceding it") without spelling out the grep/cmp invocation that produces pass/fail. AC-11's edge cases ("fatal compose error", "malformed attribute is ignored") have no executable assertion. The skill `eval:` field still references "every structured visual block" without naming the four new kinds, so a fresh agent cannot tell from the eval alone whether key-features|resources|key-decisions|phase-split coverage is part of the success bar. Several requirements (R9 subtitle, R5 whitespace preservation, R5 source-order) lack a directly traceable AC-with-command.

findings.title: Skill `eval:` field does not enumerate the four new block kinds
findings.principle_violation: Every skill has a binary eval: field describing the success check. The current eval reads 'every structured visual block in the PRD renders deterministically into the Visual abstract section' — a fresh agent reading the eval cannot determine whether `:::key-features`, `:::resources`, `:::key-decisions`, `:::phase-split` are covered, or whether the new kinds must be stripped from the PRD body. The eval is the binary contract; it must name what counts.
findings.proposed_binary_verify_step: Replace the eval line with: `eval: features/NNN-{slug}/{NNN-slug}-brief.html exists; second compose from unchanged sources is byte-identical (cmp -s passes); for each of {flow,comparison,scope,tree,key-features,resources,key-decisions,phase-split} a fixture PRD containing that block produces compiled HTML matching the documented selector (.journey, .modes-row, .scope, .cap-tree, .key-features, .resources, .key-decisions, .phase-split) inside <section id="visual-abstract"> AND the literal `:::{kind}` text does NOT appear inside <section id="prd">; sidebar TOC links resolve; rendered HTML carries a one-line policy banner reflecting config.brief.commitPolicy.`

findings.title: AC-4 hides judgement inside 'produces the documented HTML shape' parenthetical
findings.principle_violation: 'Documented HTML shape' is a description, not an assertion. The four payload phrases ("CSS-grid row of feature cards", "row of link cards with favicon + title + source-type pill", "<table> with Decision | Why | Source columns", "two-column panel") need a fresh agent to translate prose into selectors. That translation is judgement.
findings.proposed_binary_verify_step:
Split AC-4 into four selector-grep assertions. Given a fixture PRD body with one of each new block, all of these must pass:
```sh
grep -qE '<section id="visual-abstract">[\s\S]*<div class="key-features">[\s\S]*<article class="feature-card">' brief.html
grep -qE '<section id="visual-abstract">[\s\S]*<div class="resources">[\s\S]*<a class="resource-card"[^>]*>[\s\S]*<img[^>]+src="data:' brief.html
grep -qE '<section id="visual-abstract">[\s\S]*<table class="key-decisions">[\s\S]*<th[^>]*>Decision</th>[\s\S]*<th[^>]*>Why</th>[\s\S]*<th[^>]*>Source</th>' brief.html
grep -qE '<section id="visual-abstract">[\s\S]*<div class="phase-split">[\s\S]*<div class="phase-col this-phase">[\s\S]*<div class="phase-col next-phase">' brief.html
```
Freeze the selector names in the PRD so AC-4 and the implementation share one vocabulary.

findings.title: AC-11 edge-case ACs have no executable assertion
findings.principle_violation: 'Fatal compose error per § Strict rules', 'malformed attribute is ignored, not fatal', 'treated as a closing marker' — these are behavioural descriptions. None says HOW a fresh agent verifies. Exit code? stderr regex? presence of a card despite the bad attribute? Without that, AC-11 fails the binary test.
findings.proposed_binary_verify_step:
Rewrite AC-11 with three executable sub-assertions:
- **Unclosed block**: fixture PRD with `:::key-features` and no closer → `specflow:brief NNN-slug` exits non-zero AND stderr matches regex `unclosed block.*key-features.*:[0-9]+` (file:line citation).
- **Nested `:::`**: fixture PRD with `:::key-features\n- foo | bar\n:::\n` (literal `:::` line in body) → compose succeeds (exit 0); compiled HTML contains exactly one `<div class="key-features">` and the second `:::` line is absent from the HTML body (`grep -c '^:::$' brief.html` returns 0).
- **Malformed attribute**: fixture PRD with `:::resources title=` (no value) → compose succeeds (exit 0); `<div class="resources">` is present and contains no `<h3>` / `<h2>` title element (`grep -qE '<div class="resources">[^<]*<a class="resource-card"' brief.html` passes — title slot empty/skipped).

findings.title: AC-10 'visually distinct shapes' is not binary
findings.principle_violation: 'Compile to visually distinct shapes' is the canonical soft-verification anti-pattern. A fresh agent cannot run a 'visually distinct' check. The parenthetical column-heading text is the closest binary proxy but isn't framed as the assertion.
findings.proposed_binary_verify_step:
Replace AC-10 body with: Given a fixture PRD body containing both `:::scope` and `:::phase-split`, the compiled brief HTML must satisfy all four greps:
```sh
grep -qE '<div class="scope">[\s\S]*<div class="scope-col v1">[\s\S]*<div class="scope-col v2">[\s\S]*<div class="scope-col out">' brief.html
grep -qE '<div class="phase-split">[\s\S]*<div class="phase-col this-phase">[\s\S]*<div class="phase-col next-phase">' brief.html
# negative: phase-split must NOT carry the third 'out' column
! grep -qE '<div class="phase-split">[\s\S]*<div class="phase-col out">' brief.html
# count: scope renders 3 columns, phase-split renders 2
[ "$(grep -oE '<div class="scope-col [a-z0-9]+">' brief.html | wc -l)" -eq 3 ]
[ "$(grep -oE '<div class="phase-col [a-z0-9-]+">' brief.html | wc -l)" -eq 2 ]
```

findings.title: AC-1 / AC-2 are soft presence claims with no command
findings.principle_violation: '§ Visual Block Grammar lists four new block kinds' and '§ HTML Template carries CSS rule-sets for .key-features...' are presence claims. No grep is given, so a fresh agent has to find the section heading, decide what 'lists' means, and judge whether 'analogous selector names' counts. AC-2 also hedges with '(or analogous selector names)' — locking the names in is the cheap binary.
findings.proposed_binary_verify_step:
Tighten to:
```sh
# AC-1: each new block kind has a fenced example under § Visual Block Grammar
for kind in key-features resources key-decisions phase-split; do
  grep -qE "^### \`:::${kind}\`" plugins/specflow/skills/brief/SKILL.md || exit 1
done
# AC-2: each new selector class is defined inside the inline <style> block
for sel in key-features resources key-decisions phase-split; do
  grep -qE "^[[:space:]]+\\.${sel}[[:space:]{,]" plugins/specflow/skills/brief/SKILL.md || exit 1
done
# negative: no external stylesheet link added
! grep -qE '<link[^>]+rel="stylesheet"' plugins/specflow/skills/brief/SKILL.md
```
This also closes the 'analogous selector names' weasel — pick the four names, freeze them in AC-2.

findings.title: Eval-coverage matrix: three requirements lack a binary AC trace
findings.where: PRD § Requirements (R5, R7, R9) vs § Acceptance criteria
findings.principle_violation:
Goal-Driven Execution demands every requirement trace to a binary verify step. Walking R1-R10:
- R1 → AC-1, AC-2, AC-4 (binary after GDR-2/GDR-5)
- R2 → AC-1, AC-2, AC-4, AC-6 (AC-6 is binary)
- R3 → AC-1, AC-2, AC-4 (binary after GDR-2)
- R4 → AC-1, AC-2, AC-4, AC-10 (binary after GDR-2/GDR-4)
- **R5 (block contract: opener attrs, structured body, `:::` closer, whitespace preserved as authored, source-order)** → only AC-11 (closer/attribute edge cases). **No AC asserts whitespace preservation; no AC asserts source-order rendering.**
- R6 → AC-2, AC-5 (binary)
- **R7 (strip rule for new kinds from PRD body)** → AC-7 covers `:::key-features` only. The other three (`:::resources`, `:::key-decisions`, `:::phase-split`) are not asserted-stripped.
- R8 → AC-3 (binary)
- **R9 (title= AND subtitle= attribute pattern)** → AC-9 covers `title=` only. **No AC asserts `subtitle=` renders.**
- R10 → AC-8 (binary intent, no command — see severity note below)

This is the mandatory eval-coverage finding.
findings.proposed_binary_verify_step:
Add three ACs (or extend existing ones) with concrete commands:

**AC-12 (R5 whitespace + source-order)**: Given a fixture PRD with `:::key-features` followed by `:::resources` followed by `:::phase-split`, in that source order, with one feature line containing `  two-leading-spaces`:
```sh
# source order preserved
python3 -c "import re,sys; h=open('brief.html').read(); s=h.find('<section id=\"visual-abstract\">'); e=h.find('</section>',s); body=h[s:e]; idx=[body.find(c) for c in ['key-features','resources','phase-split']]; sys.exit(0 if idx==sorted(idx) and -1 not in idx else 1)"
# whitespace preserved: literal '  two-leading-spaces' appears in compiled output
grep -qE '  two-leading-spaces' brief.html
```

**AC-13 (R7 extended strip rule for all four new kinds)**: Given a fixture PRD body containing all four new blocks:
```sh
for kind in key-features resources key-decisions phase-split; do
  # extract <section id="prd"> ... </section> range; verify literal ':::kind' marker absent
  python3 -c "import sys; h=open('brief.html').read(); s=h.find('<section id=\"prd\">'); e=h.find('</section>',s); sys.exit(0 if ':::${kind}' not in h[s:e] else 1)" || exit 1
done
```

**AC-14 (R9 subtitle=)**: A `:::key-features title="Key features" subtitle="What the feature does"` block produces compiled HTML in which `grep -qE '>What the feature does<' brief.html` passes inside the `<div class="key-features">` block.

Also harden **AC-8** (R10): change to `grep -qE 'Unsupported visual block[\s\S]{0,200}<pre' brief.html` so the literal string + ordering is asserted, not described.
